methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $3M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 9 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Ouros Energy is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Ethan Loosbrock that has raised $3M+. The comparable universe includes 9 same-sector peers: 1 public (LNZA) and 8 private companies including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Given the nascent stage and limited peer comparability within narrow filters, only the stage-progression method is reliably applicable. Using total capital raised ($3M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to the next stage yields an implied valuation of $7.5M. The peer-median approach is inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables in the climate and energy sector—while 9 same-sector peers exist, fewer than 3 meet the narrow stage and valuation-tier criteria required for statistical relevance.

The triangulated valuation range is $6M (low) to $9M (high), with a median of $8M. This single-method analysis reflects meaningful uncertainty inherent in early-stage valuation. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue or unit economics data, reliance on a single methodology, and the nascent state of climate tech benchmarking. Any future round pricing should incorporate updated financial performance and refined peer comparability as the market matures.
